sources.note: Silent. Section 2 'Writing system and sounds' (p. 9) is three lines: consonant letters, vowels a e i o u, and 'When a vowel is double it is called a long vowel'. No mention of stress/accent anywhere in the text layer (a full-text search for stress/accent/syllable/penult: only a reduplication remark).

sources.note: Nothing for this language: Arifama/Meniafia appear only as reflex columns in the Papuan Tip sound-correspondence tables (ch. 6) and morphology tables; the word 'stress' occurs only in the North New Guinea lenition discussion. Bibliography names the primary phonology source: Wakefield 1975 'Miniafia phonology. TS. SIL, Ukarumpa' and n.d. 'Miniafia grammar essentials. TS.'

sources.citation: Wakefield, David C. 1975. Grammar Notes on Arifama-Miniafia. Unpublished typescript, SIL, Ukarumpa. 42 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 41148; archived file ''; = Ross 1988's 'Miniafia grammar essentials' TS)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Scanned TS scanned in full (43 pp.): stems, word classes, verb morphology, phrases, clauses, sentences. Only prosodic remarks are sentence intonation (falling declarative / rising interrogative and clause-linking rising intonation, PDF pp. 32-38). No word-stress statement; phonology was a separate 1975 TS ('Miniafia phonology') not online.

sources.note: The only phonological description of the language on record (subject: Phonology); SIL-PNG OPDs routinely include a syllable-pattern and stress paragraph - almost certainly contains the deciding sentence. Free PDF but could not be reached by automated download and absent from the Internet Archive/Common Crawl; a browser download by a human (69 KB) would settle the row.
